Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Sri Lanka's reply. The umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Dimuth Karunaratne and Pathum Nissanka will open the innings for Sri Lanka. Bilal Khan has the new ball in hand for Oman and is raring to go. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, it has been a disappointing effort with the bat by Oman. The writing is on the wall for them and it will be about delaying the inevitable. On the other hand, Dasun Shanaka will be proud of this bowling effort and now the onus is on the batters to complete the job. Back in a bit for the chase...

Ayaan Khan is in for a flash interview. He says that he played the ball to its merit which helped him score the runs he did but he feels disappointed with this total on such a track. He adds that this was a brilliant opportunity to play and showcase our talent in front of a quality Test side but the team crumbled a bit today. Adds that everybody is so supportive of the team and is enjoying our growth in this tournament.

As far as Oman are concerned, only three batters were able to reach two figures which sum up their story with the bat. They were rocked early, losing Kashyap Prajapati in the second over. They were unable to weather the storm of the Sri Lankan bowlers and were struggling at 20-4. Ayaan Khan and Jatinder Singh then got together and started the repair job for Oman. However, the latter's departure in the 21st over pegged them back them once again. In no time, they were reduced to 72-7 but Ayaan Khan stood strong and showed resistance with his knock of 41 runs. He was running out of partners and in the end, fell prey to Wanindu Hasaranga. His dismissal meant the tail was unable to take Oman over 100.

Wanindu Hasaranga finishes with another five-wicket haul and this has been a dominating bowling effort by Sri Lanka! They have skittled Oman out for a paltry total of 98 runs! It was Lahiru Kumara who set the tone early for them by striking in his first over. At the other end, Kasun Rajitha backed it up to put Oman in early trouble. Both new ball pacers kept bowling disciplined lines and lengths and vindicated their skipper's decision to bowl first. Coming off a six-wicket haul in the last outing, Wanindu Hasaranga ran through the Oman lower order by striking thrice in a single over. Ayaan Khan did make them work hard for his wicket but Hasaranga accounted for him as well. He then went to wrap up the Oman innings by trapping Bilal Khan in fron of the stumps.

OUT! PLUMB! That's a wrap for Oman as Wanindu Hasaranga dismisses Bilal Khan to grab yet another fifer. Fuller one in middle, Bilal Khan looks to play the slog sweep but misses out completely as the ball hits him bang in front of the middle. Oman gets bundled out for just 94 in little under 30 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to start as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. The Sri Lankan players take their respective field positions and they are joined by the two Oman openers. Jatinder Singh and Kashyap Prajapati will open the innings for Oman. Kasun Rajitha will start with the new ball for Sri Lanka. Let's play...

The first ball in this crucial Group B fixture is moments away but before that, the match officials and the two sets of players will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Oman's first followed by the national anthem of Sri Lanka.

Zeeshan Maqsood, the captain of Oman, says that batting first wouldn't make a lot of difference as it's just the first few overs they need to negotiate. He adds that people back in the country are happy and they are backing them. Informs that they are playing with the same team.

Dasun Shanaka, the skipper of Sri Lanka, says they will bowl first because of the overcast conditions. He adds that they are a confident side but they can not take Oman lightly. They are going in with the same squad.
Oman (Unchanged Playing XI) - Kashyap Prajapati, Jatinder Singh, Aqib Ilyas, Shoaib Khan, Zeeshan Maqsood (C), Mohammad Nadeem, Ayaan Khan, Naseem Khushi (WK), Jay Odedra, Fayyaz Butt, Bilal Khan.

Sri Lanka (Unchanged Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Dimuth Karunaratne, Kusal Mendis (WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Dasun Shanaka (C), Dhananjaya de Silva, Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, Kasun Rajitha, Lahiru Kumara.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Sri Lanka and they have opted to BOWL first.

On the other hand, Sri Lanka also started their campaign on an expected high, as they thumped UAE by a massive margin of 175 runs. Everyone contributed for the Islanders in the first game. Wanindu Hasaranga was a standout as he took six wickets and ripped apart the UAE's batting lineup. Skipper Dasun Shanaka would be counting on his batters and the bowlers to put up an impressive effort in this game as well. Can the Islanders dethrone Oman from the top of the table, or will Oman keep up to their reputation as giant killers? Let's see as the toss and team updates follow.

Oman is on an all-time high after inflicting defeats on a full-member nation in Ireland and the UAE in their opening two fixtures. Oman has bowled superbly so far and has restricted two solid batting lineups for a below-par score on these batting paradises in Zimbabwe. Oman is well placed on top of the tree in group B and would be looking to seal a spot in the next stage with a victory today.

Hello and welcome to all our viewers! We are all set to face a thrilling encounter as high-flying Oman faces the Asian giants in Sri Lanka at the Queens Sports Club, Bulawayo, in match no. 11 of the ongoing ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifiers.
...MATCH DAY...

The group stages of the ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifiers 2023 are at a crucial stage now and the Super Six are starting to take shape. In Match 11, a strong Sri Lankan side will take on a resilient Oman team that has already shown its quality in the tournament. Oman have played two matches and won them quite comfortably with both batting and bowling. Their bowlers have been excellent as Fayyaz Butt and Bilal Khan are their frontline pacers who get those early breakthroughs while Jay Odedra and skipper Zeeshan Maqsood handle the spin department well. Their batters are also in good touch as Shoaib Khan, Aqib Ilyas, Jatinder Singh, and Kashyap Prajapati ​​​​​​ have all got runs under their belt and although they were tested in the last game, they didn't give in under the pressure and emerged victorious. They will surely back themselves to cause a huge upset here. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, had a good break after destroying the UAE in their first game. They have probably the strongest side and will hope to get back where they belong. They have Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka at the top while Dhananjaya de Silva, Charith Asalanka, and Sadeera Samarawickrama who scored an excellent fifty in the last game make up a solid middle order. Their spin duo of Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana can get through any batting order and the former showed his class with a six-wicket haul against UAE. Dushmantha Chameera, Kasun Rajitha, and Lahiru Kumara are their fast bowlers who will be a real threat to Oman batters along with young Matheesha Pathirana,  who is still settling into this format. They would hope to make it two wins in a row and avoid any scares. Let's see who comes out on top.
